output.brief:
The wrong expiry dates did not come from the agency operators or the printer firmware. Printer records show no overrides on any of the 47 Veltranol jobs. The printers printed exactly what they received. The 30 jobs through 3 Oct, including four after the firmware change, were correct. From 4 Oct the incoming data said a 36-month shelf life, and 17 jobs ran with expiry a year too late. Two of those were on Line 1 day shift, run by permanent staff.

The ERP shows Regulatory Affairs entered a 36-month value on 3 Oct, but it was dated to take effect in March 2027. The 24-month value was still the one in force. The integration service should not have used the 36. Why it did is still unexplained, and its configuration should be checked. Even so, the fault is in the data, not the operators.

Next steps:
1. Drop the warnings and the removal of agency operators. They would punish the wrong people.
2. Reset the Veltranol shelf-life record.
3. Hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the two in the warehouse.
4. Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup.
5. Inspect retained cartons for other products whose records changed in October.
6. Have IT and the vendor explain why the future-dated value was read.

I'm fairly sure of the cause. I can't yet say whether other products are affected.
